proposed.explanation:
Your friend's numbers are off. The FY2025 consolidated net profit is 22,578,063,000 EGP (about 22.6 billion), not 225.9 billion. The FY2024 figure was 10,111,328,000 EGP (about 10.1 billion). So profit more than doubled (roughly 2.2×), not ten-fold. The friend likely misread the thousands-unit table.

The financials do show genuine strength: operating revenue grew ~31% to 106.7 billion EGP, net profit more than doubled, EPS rose from 4.79 to 11.93 EGP, and total equity grew from 45.9 billion to 63.7 billion EGP. These are positive signals.

However, I would not put all 50,000 EGP into ETEL for two reasons. First, the diversification rule caps any single holding at 50% of total portfolio value (71,292.50 EGP), which limits additional ETEL to about 101 shares. Second, the evidence is limited: we have only two years of results, no dividend information (important for a retirement goal), no debt breakdown, no forward guidance, and no context on whether the profit jump is sustainable or driven by one-off items. With a medium risk tolerance and a 5-year horizon, concentrating further in one stock is unwise.

A modest addition of 50 shares (cost ≈ 7,097.50 EGP) raises your holding to 200 shares (≈ 28,390 EGP, about 40% of the portfolio) while keeping 42,902.50 EGP in cash for diversification. This lets you participate in the company's strong recent performance without over-concentrating. Monitor future reports for dividend policy, debt levels, and whether the profit growth is recurring before considering a larger position.
